# Settings and Themes

Use **Find a setting…** to jump to a control. Theme and keyboard bindings are browser-local. Provider connections and launcher visibility belong to your account. [Settings](clank://settings).

## Files, Editor and agent access

**Permissions → Your file access** shows what you can open in Files and Editor. Administrators share a **Location** through **People**, with **Browse / download** or **Modify** access. **Operation approvals** shows saved agent approvals and when they expire.

The owner and administrators can set **Permissions → Full filesystem access** for their own accounts. **Files and Editor** and **Agents for this account** are separate switches. On uses the host OS account’s permissions. Off uses existing folder grants. **Account → Full access** enables models and optional tools where offered.

## Account and administration

Set up your authenticator under **Account → Two-Factor Authentication**. For a provider login, see [[Accounts and Models]]. Administrators manage scoped API tokens at `/api/tokens`.

Check **Logging → Storage inventory**, or use the administrator’s **System → Stack health**, **Terminal Logs** and **Data Backup**. For what backups cover, see [[Recovery#Restore an installation|Restore an installation]].

**Tokenomics** lets you opt into changes such as reusing exact repeated Browser snapshot text. Check the effective settings there and observed usage under [[Usage and Stats]].

## Connect an MCP tool server

As an administrator, open **Settings → Integrations → MCP Tool Server**. Select **stdio** for a command, arguments and environment on the host, or **SSE** or **Streamable HTTP** for a server URL. Put credentials in the connection settings. Choose **Save**, complete **Authorize** if prompted and check the tool list. A local command uses the host’s access. A remote tool receives the data you pass to it.

## Change appearance

Open [Appearance](clank://settings/appearance). Choose **Solid** to stop background motion. **Copal navigation** restores a hidden Journal shortcut. [Shortcuts](clank://settings/shortcuts) shows your bindings.

New supported workbooks and decks use the current theme. To change an existing one, see [[Deliverables#Edit a slide deck|Apply the current theme]]. **Reduce motion in generated deliverables** is an account preference.

## Google Emoji Drift artwork

Select the effect to review consent. **Allow** permits artwork acquisition. Emoji Drift and Emoji Rain use Kene Weave until consent and local artwork are available. **Refresh artwork status** shows the installation and update state. Pause or resume weekly updates there, or **Revoke emoji artwork consent**. See [[Credits and Included Components]].

# Settings and Themes

Settings owns configuration and appearance. Theme lives here — there is no
separate theme applet.

Open [Settings](clank://settings).

## Panels

| Panel | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| [Appearance](clank://settings/appearance) | Theme, colors, background effects |
| [Providers](clank://settings/providers) | Model providers and keys |
| [History](clank://settings/history) | Memory and retention budgets |
| [File access](clank://settings/file-access) | What the assistant may touch |

Settings panels are reachable by direct navigation. Opening a panel from a
link focuses it; it never closes a window you already had open.

## Themes

Themes change colors, backgrounds and effects across the whole shell. The
theme picker shows live previews. Custom accent colors are available on every
theme, and you can save your own named themes (up to eight) and share them as
JSON.

Background / Effect chooses the decorative background. The shipped effects
are: Solid, Clanker Signal Routes, Shipibo Kene-Inspired Signal Weave,
Clanker LCARS, Clanker Gem Drift, Clanker Emoji Drift, Clanker Matrix Rain,
Clanker Emoji Rain, Clanker LCARS Status Sweep, Dots, Synapse, Rain,
Constellations, Perlin Flow, Petals, Sparkles and Embers. Each effect that
supports it exposes an effect color, an Intensity slider and a Size slider;
effects without those controls hide them.

Background effects are decorative. On machines where an effect is too heavy
it can be turned off without changing the rest of the theme.

## Typography and accessibility

Appearance also controls typography: a font choice, a density setting
(comfortable, compact, spacious) and a UI text-size scale that is independent
of the active theme. A frosted-glass toggle softens panels where the theme
supports it. These are readability controls, not decoration.

## What settings does not do

- It does not migrate your documents.
- It does not change other accounts' settings.
- It does not require a restart for appearance changes.

[[Accounts and Models]] covers provider setup in more detail.
